parts.text: Use Table 1.1 to help you to answer parts (i), (ii) and (iii).

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
With which TPP member did New Zealand have the largest deficit on its trade in goods
in the year ended June 2015? Explain your answer.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
New Zealand’s balance of trade in goods plus its services balance was estimated at
NZ$2400m for the year ended June 2015. Calculate New Zealand’s services balance.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: What two other items are needed to calculate New Zealand’s current account balance?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Use the principle of comparative advantage to explain why New Zealand is likely to benefit
from membership of the TPP.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain the likely effects of the removal of protection on the incomes of Canada’s farmers.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss whether China joining the TPP would be likely to be of overall benefit to existing TPP
members.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Using an example of each, explain the differences between direct progressive taxes and
indirect regressive taxes.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Discuss whether a sugar tax or an educational campaign on healthy eating is more likely to
reduce child obesity.

text: In March 2016, the United Kingdom government announced that it will introduce a ‘sugar tax’ on
the producers of fizzy soft drinks in order to reduce child obesity.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
State and explain two factors of production needed for the manufacture of chocolate. Explain
the benefits of specialisation in the manufacture of chocolate.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Analyse the likely effects on the global price of chocolate of the reported changes in 2015.
Discuss the most effective way that the price of chocolate might be stabilised.

text: In 2015, it was reported that the global demand for chocolate was projected to increase but it was
unlikely that the global supply of cocoa beans, required to produce chocolate, would increase.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain the main causes of changes in the general price level in your country, or any other
country with which you are familiar.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Discuss whether monetary policy alone is the best way for a government to correct inflation.
